provenance.method: Native text extracted directly from the PPTX. All 42 embedded artwork images inspected individually and their meaningful readable content transcribed. Selected slides cross-checked independently.

Do not borrow instructions from another topic.

shared_style.setting_and_audience: Australian mine sites, FIFO camp rooms, workshops, outback roads and familiar social settings. The depicted audience is largely adult workers and mates.
shared_style.illustration: Heavy black ink contours, comic caricature, expressive faces and practical props. Some pages use relatively detailed cross-hatching; slides 16, 18 and 27 are brighter, simpler poster cartoons.
shared_style.colour: Safety yellow and warm cream dominate. Dusty ochre, brown, grey and muted high-vis orange/green support worksite scenes. Red flags incorrect examples. Pink is used around the nurse topic.
shared_style.materials: Grubby paper, chipped yellow signs, ripped/taped corners, bolts, hazard-stripe borders and small hand-drawn warning symbols.
shared_style.lettering: Large condensed uppercase black headings. Smaller black instructional copy with selective bold phrases. Source lettering is baked into most images and contains some errors.
shared_style.characters: Recurring type rather than a reliably locked individual: broad-faced adult workers, often moustached, in hard hats and high-vis workwear. Other roles include nurse, safety representative, emergency personnel, pub patrons and family members. Do not silently treat varying source faces as one fixed character.
shared_style.humour: Exaggerated consequences, Australian colloquialism, mock official language, mechanical/body metaphors, overconfident shortcuts, social embarrassment and deadpan warnings.

source_record.title: DON’T LOSE YOUR FACE! THE ROUGH-AS-GUTS GUIDE TO ANGLE GRINDERS

format.layout: Three horizontal step panels above three checklist cards; yellow pinned title banner; taped sheets on battered workshop wall.
format.style: Distressed vintage comic poster; thick black outlines, muted yellow hi-vis, blue and cream panels.

panels.heading: GUARD YOUR LIFE (FIT THE GUARD)
text: Keep the bloody guard on. Taking it off to fit a bigger wheel makes you an idiot, not efficient.
It’s a grenade, not a tool. That disc spins at 11,000 RPM. If it binds and explodes.
speech: It fits if I force it!
panels.observed_scene: Grinning hard-hatted male worker in yellow hi-vis holds an angle grinder fitted with an oversized unguarded wheel. A smaller detached guard is labelled beside a bin of metal scrap; separate scrap bucket at right.

panels.heading: THE TWO-HAND TANGO (GRIP & STANCE)
text: One hand is for cowboys. Leave the 10-gallon hat at home and grip the tool with BOTH hands like you actually want to keep your fingers.
Stand clear of the kick. Position your body to the side of the cut. When it grabs, you want it flying past your ribs, not through them.

panels.heading: SPARK CONTROL (THE FIRING LINE)

Check the test. Don’t pack up and bolt for the grass don’t mix with a 1,200-degree shower of molten metal. Donietly smouldering in the dark.

source_record.title: SILENCE THE WATERFALL! THE ROUGH-AS-GUTS GUIDE TO 4AM CAMP NEIGHBOURS

format.layout: Yellow metal title sign with bed/clock, crossed pick and skull warning icons; three horizontal steps and three bottom checklist cards.
format.style: Distressed taped comic notices on rusty mine-camp wall; hard-hatted yellow-hi-vis workers.

panels.heading: THE THERMAL ACOUSTIC RESONANCE (THE 4AM WAKE-UP CALL)
text: Camp donga walls are structurally identical to wet tissue paper. When your neighbor wakes up at 04:00 to clear their bladder, the sound resonance transforms a simple bodily function into a roaring, high-pressure industrial waterfall. Brace your ears, deploy earplugs early, and prepare your mind for the acoustic onslaught.
speech: I CAN HEAR EVERYTHING! IT’S A FLOOD!
panels.observed_scene: Worker lies awake in bed under grey bedding with hands clamped over ears. Huge yellow sound-wave graphic travels through thin shared wall.

panels.heading: HUNT THE TACTICAL AIM ANGLE (THE PORCELAIN MUFFLER)
text: If you are the one waking up early, exhibit basic operational courtesy. Do not aim directly into the center water trap like you are trying to drill a hole through the plumbing. Utilize the “Silent Rim Strategy”—angle the stream against the dry side porcelain curve to suppress decibel levels and preserve your neighbor’s REM sleep.
speech: Angle it for silence! preserve neighbour’s REM!
panels.observed_scene: Diagram of open toilet with orange arrow pointing toward inside rim. At right hard-hatted worker stands urinating into a toilet, illustrating stream angle.

panels.heading: GET THE HELL BACK TO SLEEP (THE WALL THUMP RECOVERY)
text: If the noise breaches your auditory defenses, do not launch a verbal war or scream through the vent. Deliver one sharp, controlled, structural thump to the shared drywall with the heel of your work boot. This site code instantly signals the operator on the other side to throttle down their volumetric flow rate immediately.
speech: Throttle down! Universal site code!
Deliver one sharp, controlled, structural thump!
panels.observed_scene: A yellow-hi-vis worker raises a booted leg and kicks the shared wall on the left. A cropped orange-clad person is visible at the wall centre. A separate startled yellow-hi-vis man on the right holds a hand at his chest. An impact starburst marks the wall thump.

items.label: NO CENTER-POOL DRILLING
text: Do not stand dead-center and let fly with maximum force. Your neighbor does not need a live broadcast of your fluid dynamics at four in the morning.
items.observed_scene: Worker holds a long hose with high-pressure jet producing a large splash.

items.label: NO VENTILATION SLAM DANCES
text: Do not slam the plastic bathroom door or yank the exhaust fan cord like you’re starting a chainsaw. Move like a stealth operative.
items.observed_scene: Worker pushes/slams bathroom door beside wall-mounted extractor fan and pull cord; red X.

items.label: NO REVENGE WATERWORKS

panels.heading: THE DROP BEAR BLITZ
text: THE ZIP-TIE SPANNER: Attach spiky zip-ties to your helmet. Looks ridiculous, might work.
THE VEGEMITE ANGLE: Daub Vegemite behind your ears. Some say it repels them.
THE COUGH-GUT: A deep, continuous cough is said to show weakness. Keep doing it.
THE LAST RESORT: Grab a sturdy stick. It’s too late now. Just pray.

panels.heading: THE CASSOWARY RUMBLE
text: THE GIANT’S KICK: Watch out for that single claw. It’s a lethal weapon. Avoid.
THE CASQUE DANCE: The casque on their head is solid. Don’t engage. Be a small, invisible person.
THE SPEED BUMP: Do not try to feed it. They’re fast and remember faces.
THE REVERSE MARCH: If it approaches, make yourself small and back away. Do not turn your back.

panels.heading: CROCODILE BAIT
text: THE LURKING MENACE: Stay back. The murky water hides the real threat.
THE FOOT-TO-SNOUT: Check your steps. A log is never just a log. It’s a snout.
BAIT THE LINE: Don’t put your own feet near the edge. Use bait. Live or otherwise.
THE LAST LOOK: Look twice before approaching any water edge. A second look could save you.

panels.heading: THE GARAGE SNAKE
text: THE LOOKOUT: Always check before you step or reach. Especially near tools or boots.
LEAVE IT ALONE: Red-Bellied Black Snakes are common. They generally just want space.

panels.heading: GEAR UP FOR THE BITE (PREVENTION & PPE)
text: Chemicals don’t give second chances. Splash goggles, a full-face shield, and heavy-duty nitrile gauntlets are your only line of defence against a lifelong blind spot.

panels.heading: RUN FOR THE RIG (IMMEDIATE FLUSHING)
text: Every second is a layer of skin. If you get hit, do not hesitate, do not curse—sprint directly to the nearest emergency safety shower and eyewash station.
Smash the paddle. Slap stream. Keep your eyes right in the water jets and roll your eyeballs around in all directions for a minimum of 15 non-stop minutes to dilute the burn.

panels.heading: FORGET YOUR SHYNESS (PRY AND FLUSH)

Modesty won’t save your hide. Cut or tear contaminated clothing away immediately while the high-volume safety shower drenches you from head to toe.

source_record.subtitle_banner: DON’T GET MANGLED!

panels.heading: RESPECT THE BITE (IDENTIFY THE PINCH)
text: If it hinges or slides, it wants to eat you. A pinch point is any gap where moving parts come together—like heavy linkages, tailgates, or conveyor rollers.
Keep your digits clear. Never place your fingers or limbs between unblocked moving components, because steel always wins against bone.
BITE ZONE
panels.observed_scene: Yellow hi-vis worker in hard hat and green gloves points toward excavator linkage; black/yellow striped pivot guard and red arrow identify pinch zone; skull icon.

panels.heading: WATCH THE LINE OF FIRE (CRUSH ZONES)
text: Never trust a hydraulic seal to hold. A blown hose or a sudden drop in pressure will slam a massive blade, bucket, or truck tray down in a split second.
Chock it or pin it flat. Always drop implements flat to the dirt or physically lock them out using certified mechanical safety pins and stands before crawling underneath.
panels.observed_scene: Large mine haul truck beside tall concrete wall; a worker occupies narrow gap near rear wheel/wall while another stands away; red ground stripe marks line-of-fire area; leaning stand/prop at truck; lightning icon.

panels.heading: HANDS OFF THE LOAD (SUSPENDED CARGO)
text: A swinging hook has no friends. Never use your bare hands to guide or push an active overhead crane load or a load slung from a forklift.
Use your tag lines. Stand well clear of the drop zone and use a long, high-vis tag line rope to steer the cargo smoothly onto the deck.
STOOD DOWN

source_record.title: DON’T GET BURIED IN THE DUNES! THE ROUGH-AS-GUTS GUIDE TO TYRE PRESSURES & SAND RECOVERY
source_record.format_orientation: Portrait industrial cartoon poster; three stacked horizontal step panels printed as steps 1, 3 and 4; three bottom checklist boxes.
source_record.visual_style: Weathered grey metal wall, pinned and taped yellow heading, distressed white/yellow instruction panels; worksite warning signs; sandy off-road vehicle scenes and red prohibition marks.

panels.heading: DROP THE PSI (EXTEND YOUR FOOTPRINT)
text: Highway pressures are sand traps. Trying to push through soft powder at 38 PSI is like trying to drive through wet cement with pizza cutters.
Go low and go early. Drop your tyres straight down to 15–18 PSI before you hit the soft track to instantly double your tyre footprint and float over the sand.

panels.heading: DEPLOY THE TRACKS (MAXTRAX PROTOCOLS)
text: Stop spinning and digging. If you lose forward momen, drop the throttle immediately—spinning your wheels just digs a deeper grave for your diffs.
Clear the path and wedge them tight. Dig out the sand in front of all four tyres, wedge your recovery tracks firmly under a spend the afternoon jacking up a crawl out slow.

panels.heading: MIND THE REBOUND (SAFE SNATCHING)
text: A flying hitch is an absolute killer. If you need a snatch strap recovery, never pull from a standard tow ball or an unrated factory tie-down loop.
Rig it right. Use a minimum of two rated recovery points, a dampener blanket over the middle of the strap, and a soft shackle to keep flying steel links out of your cabin window.

items.label: NO WHEEL SPINNING
text: Do NOT dump the clutch. (Spinning your tyres in soft sand just drops your chassis rails straight onto the deck, making the recovery twice as hard).

items.label: NO UNRATED TOW BALLS

items.label: NO HIGH-SPEED CORNERING
text: Do NOT speed on low air. (Driving fast with low PSI causes extreme sidewall heat build-up and guarantees a rolled tyre bead on the first sharp corner).

source_record.title: SPLAT IS NOT A SAFETY PLAN! THE ROUGH-AS-GUTS GUIDE TO HEIGHTS & LADDERS
source_record.format_orientation: Portrait industrial safety poster; three stacked instruction panels with a three-column bottom checklist containing internal text as well as outside captions.
source_record.visual_style: Grey stained workshop wall; large yellow hazard-striped headline; taped white/yellow panels; thick black comic outlines and exaggerated high-vis workers. Red NO labels and red crosses dominate the checklist.

panels.heading: THE THREE POINTS OF CONTACT (HOLD ON TIGHT)
text: Keep your paws anchored. You need THREE limbs glued to the ladder at all times. Your teeth do not count.
Gravity doesn’t blink. The moment you try to carry an entire workshop up a rung, you’re auditing the concrete.
speech: I got this!
panels.observed_scene: A grinning miner stands near an open A-frame ladder, carrying a heavy toolbox in one hand and a pie in the other. His body leans forward with movement marks. A skull icon appears beside the heading.

panels.heading: CRATES ARE FOR MILK (NOT FOR SCAFFOLDING)
text: Step away from the plastic. Stacking milk crates doesn’t make you an engineer; it makes you a statistic.
Use a proper platform. If your scaffolding looks like a wobbly Jenga tower, pack it up. Use a certified platform.
speech: Close enough!
panels.observed_scene: At left, three red plastic milk crates are precariously stacked under a metal roof or beam with a hand on its edge. At centre, a miner balances standing in a wheelbarrow while a black cat walks beside it. Two small milk-crate icons accompany the heading.

panels.heading: THE RUNAWAY ANCHOR (CHOOSE WISELY)
text: Don’t tie off to the ute. Your anchor needs to be solid structure, not a vehicle your apprentice is driving to lunch.
Test the hold. If your life relies on a bumper bar, a tree branch, or a loose chimney, you’re playing Russian roulette.
panels.observed_scene: A miner is falling or sliding off the edge of a roof while a rope from his waist runs to the rear of a white ute. The ute drives away in a cloud of exhaust/dust with another worker at its wheel. A small loaded-truck icon appears in the heading.

items.label: NO “LEANING TOWERS”
text: Do NOT use an A-frame ladder as ladder. ( slippery metal beam at a dangerous 45-degree angle.
Do NOT use an A-frame ladder as an extension ladder. (They are built to stand alone. Lean it, and it will slide like ice.)
items.observed_scene: An open A-frame ladder stands below/against a long diagonal silver metal beam. The internal text describes a slippery beam; the lower caption describes misuse as an extension ladder.

items.label: NO “SHE’LL BE RIGHT” STRETCHES
text: Do NOT over three metres to the side from a steady ladder to fix a screw, → his center of gravity completely off-balance.
Do NOT overreach. (Move the bloody ladder. Saving thirty seconds isn’t worth three months in a full-body cast.)
items.observed_scene: A high-vis worker high on an angled ladder stretches his torso and arms far to the side. An arrow points towards him.

items.label: NO “BUNGEE JUMPING WITHOUT THE BUNGEE”
text: Do NOT use uninspected forn shock absorber an a carabiner held together by electrical tape.
Do NOT use uninspected fall gear. (If it has already taken a fall, or sits rotting in the ute, throw it out.)
items.observed_scene: A yellow/orange fall-arrest lanyard with hooks has a frayed black energy-absorber section, exposed ragged fibres and improvised binding.
